ordered_diagnoses: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries

s1.syndrome_frame: Abnormal cardiac conduction and morphology with unusual cardiac positioning
salient_findings: Apex of the heart located at the right side of the chest
Right atrium and right ventricle on the left side and the left atrium and left ventricle on the right side on echocardiogram
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 80s
Referred for cardiac evaluation after abnormal electrocardiogram
No previous medical records available
Denies history of chest pain
Physical examination showed hepatic dullness in the left subcostal region
Initial ECG showed wide complex rhythm at rate of 76 beats/min with right bundle branch block morphology
QRS duration of 120 milliseconds
Negative P waves with pathological Q waves in leads I and aVL
Positive P waves in lead V1
Biphasic P waves in leads V2 through V6
Pathological Q waves in leads V5 and V6
Transthoracic Echocardiogram showed abnormal cardiac positioning

shortlist.label: Dextrocardia with situs solitus

shortlist.label: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries
shortlist.why_kept: Echocardiogram shows right atrium and right ventricle laid on the left side and the left atrium and left ventricle on the right side

shortlist.label: Dextrocardia with situs inversus
shortlist.why_kept: Possible explanation for the abnormal cardiac positioning and hepatic dullness in the left subcostal region

shortlist.label: Levocardia with mirror-image dextrocardia
shortlist.why_kept: Alternative explanation for the abnormal cardiac positioning, although less likely

shortlist.label: Ebstein's anomaly
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of the abnormal ECG findings, including the wide QRS complex and pathological Q waves

raw.rationale: The patient's physical examination revealed the apex of the heart located at the right side of the chest, accompanied by hepatic dullness in the left subcostal region, and the transthoracic echocardiogram showed the right atrium and right ventricle on the left side and the left atrium and left ventricle on the right side, which is consistent with dextrocardia. The presence of situs solitus is suggested by the location of the liver (hepatic dullness) on the left side, indicating normal abdominal organ positioning.

rejected.label: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries
rejected.why: This condition typically involves abnormal great vessel positioning, which is not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Dextrocardia with situs inversus
rejected.why: Situs inversus would imply that the abdominal organs are also reversed, but the liver is on the left, suggesting situs solitus

rejected.label: Levocardia with mirror-image dextrocardia
rejected.why: The patient's heart is described as being on the right side, which is not consistent with levocardia

rejected.label: Ebstein's anomaly
rejected.why: While Ebstein's anomaly can involve right bundle branch block, it does not typically cause the heart to be positioned on the right side of the chest
